prTitle: Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema
head: 1950a511026d520a7329c7b6b9ee60a4af8f8b55

prOriginalConhecido.nota: Found via gh pr list search on the title (branch 35564-client-authz-schema). Its single commit is the benchmark head 1950a511026d; merged as 7e5540896b (rebase), so merged code equals the benchmark head. Files later moved to admin/fgap/ and authorization/fgap/ (May 2025).

tps.bug: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.
tps.evidenciaOpus: ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission (ClientPermissionsV2.java:214-222) only falls back to the all-clients type resource when no per-client resource exists. Per-client resources are created without a type (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104), so DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:71-80 evaluates only that resource's policies and the all-clients grant is never consulted once a per-client permission exists.
tps.evidenciaAstra: The newly added ClientPermissionsV2.java:214-224 selects the all-clients resource only when the target client's resource is absent; otherwise it evaluates only that client's resource and returns false without a global fallback (line 234). AdminPermissionsSchema.java:103-110 creates individual resources without a type, so DefaultPolicyEvaluator.java:70-87 does not automatically include the all-clients resource's policies. Consequently, a legitimate global manage/configure grant can stop working when a separate permission creates a resource for that client.
